candidates.statement: All biological products regulated under section 351 of the PHS Act must be evaluated to assure 77 that the product is safe, pure, and potent, 6 that the continued safety, purity, and potency is 78 assured, 7 and that quality is intact. 8 Potency assays are critical in ensuring that a product is 79 capable of functioning as intended and are performed during lot release testing, comparability 80 studies (Refs. 4 - 5), and stability testing (Ref. 6). REGULATORY FRAMEWORK 75 • Potency Expectations for Licensed ACTIMPs: Biologics license applications (BLAs) 85 for products regulated under section 351 of the PHS Act must contain, among other 86 things, data demonstrating that the product is potent, and that the continued potency of 87 the product is assured. 9 FDA regulations allow for considerable flexibility in 88 determining the appropriate measurement(s) of potency for each product. Potency refers 89 to the ability or capacity of the product to achieve the intended therapeutic effect; 90 therefore, the suitability of assays to measure potency is evaluated on a case-by-case 91 basis to account for product-specific attributes. All potency assays used for lot release 92 testing of licensed biological products must comply with applicable regulations, 93 including applicable Biological Product and Current Good Manufacturing Practice

candidates.statement: • Vectored ACTIMPs, including those based on viral vectors, bacterial vectors, 285 DNA, or RNA, depend on two biological activities to induce their intended effect: 286 the ability to transfer a genetic sequence to a cell, and the intended biological 287 effect of the expressed gene sequence. Therefore, potency assays for these types 288 of ACTIMPs should incorporate a quantitative potency bioassay either through a 289 protein expression assay (when justified by evidence of a direct relationship 290 between the level of expressed protein and its immunological activity), or through 291 a bioassay that measures immune responses to the expressed protein (for example, 292 the ability of vector-transduced APCs to activate target antigen-specific T cells). 293
